response.sql: WITH actor_counts AS (SELECT f.film_id, COUNT(fa.actor_id) AS actor_count FROM film AS f LEFT JOIN film_actor AS fa ON fa.film_id = f.film_id GROUP BY f.film_id), first_average AS (SELECT AVG(actor_count) AS avg_count FROM actor_counts), first_cut AS (SELECT ac.actor_count, fa.avg_count AS avg_first FROM actor_counts AS ac CROSS JOIN first_average AS fa WHERE ac.actor_count > fa.avg_count), second_average AS (SELECT AVG(actor_count) AS avg_count FROM first_cut), final_cut AS (SELECT fc.actor_count, fc.avg_first, sa.avg_count AS avg_second FROM first_cut AS fc CROSS JOIN second_average AS sa WHERE fc.actor_count > sa.avg_count) SELECT COALESCE(SUM(actor_count), 0) AS total_actor_count, AVG(actor_count - avg_first) AS avg_excess_first, AVG(actor_count - avg_second) AS avg_excess_second FROM final_cut

assumptions.assumption: A film with no film_actor rows has zero actors. Whether an absent cast record means zero actors or missing cast data is unresolved.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat films with no film_actor rows as having missing actor counts, so exclude them from both averages.
